about: Hand-researched outcomes for finished ALS studies, used by scripts/fetch-registry.mjs. Keyed by NCT ID. verdict is one of: Met primary endpoint, Missed primary endpoint, No benefit shown (exploratory study with no formal primary endpoint), Mixed results, Inconclusive, Stopped: no benefit, Stopped: safety, Stopped: slow enrollment, Stopped: business or funding, Extension or access study, Safety study, Not a treatment study, No results found. summary says what happened in plain words; source is the checked publication or report it rests on (null only for facts that are part of the registry record itself or widely documented, e.g. a drug's market withdrawal). Studies not listed here get an automatic outcome from the registry (its stop reason, posted results and linked publications).

NCT00021697.summary: Dextromethorphan/quinidine (AVP-923) reduced pseudobulbar affect (uncontrolled laughing or crying) more than either drug alone. A symptom treatment, not a disease-slowing one.

NCT00573443.summary: Dextromethorphan/quinidine reduced pseudobulbar affect episodes in people with ALS or MS; this trial supported the drug's approval (Nuedexta) for pseudobulbar affect.

NCT00386464.summary: Crossover trial of starting night-time non-invasive ventilation early, in patients with mild breathing involvement. No results were posted or found in a literature search.

NCT00047723.summary: Minocycline did not help and appeared harmful: function declined about 25% faster on minocycline than on placebo.

NCT00035815.summary: Two years of subcutaneous IGF-1 gave no benefit on muscle strength compared with placebo.

NCT00125203.summary: In 20 patients, botulinum toxin B injected into the salivary glands reduced drooling for about four weeks without significant side effects. A symptom treatment.

NCT00136110.summary: Valproate did not improve survival or slow functional decline in 163 patients.

NCT00353665.summary: Memantine showed no effect on functional decline over 12 months in 63 patients; the trial was small, so a modest effect could not be ruled out.

NCT00330681.summary: Edaravone's first phase 3 missed its primary endpoint across all patients. A post hoc analysis pointed to earlier, more typical patients, which the later MCI186-19 trial tested and confirmed.

NCT00349622.summary: Despite an early signal, the phase 3 stage (513 patients) found no slowing of functional decline, and ceftriaxone caused more gallbladder and liver problems (12% vs 0% on placebo).

NCT00372879.summary: Small crossover trial of high-dose vitamin E for muscle cramps. No results were posted or found.

NCT00415519.summary: Exploratory study in 25 patients with more advanced ALS (Japanese severity grade 3): function declined about equally on edaravone and placebo.

NCT00424463.summary: Double-blind extension of edaravone's first phase 3, testing whether continued treatment sustained any effect; published as exploratory.

NCT01492686.summary: In patients selected for early, typically progressing ALS, IV edaravone slowed functional decline by about a third over 24 weeks. This trial led to FDA approval (Radicava) in 2017.

NCT04577404.summary: Open-label safety study of oral edaravone in 185 patients: no new safety concerns over 48 weeks. It supported FDA approval of the oral form (Radicava ORS) in 2022.

NCT04569084.summary: Tested whether daily oral edaravone beats the approved on/off schedule. Stopped in 2023 when an interim analysis showed no difference (futility).

NCT05568615.summary: Open-label safety extension of oral edaravone in Japan (15 patients), run until the drug was on the market there.

NCT05178810.summary: Ferrer's oral edaravone (FAB122) did not slow functional decline over 48 weeks, and showed no survival benefit; it was safe.

NCT00444613.summary: Ultra-high-dose methylcobalamin (vitamin B12) missed both primary endpoints (time to death or ventilation, and function). A post hoc look at patients enrolled within a year of onset suggested benefit, which led to the JETALS trial.

NCT00445172.summary: Long-term open-label extension of Eisai's methylcobalamin trial.

NCT03548311.summary: JETALS: in patients enrolled within a year of onset and with moderate progression, ultra-high-dose methylcobalamin slowed functional decline over 16 weeks compared with placebo.

NCT00833820.summary: Small sham-controlled trial of magnetic stimulation of the motor cortex. A Cochrane review of the rTMS trials in ALS found no clear benefit over sham.

NCT00706147.summary: Small trial (36 patients) in rapidly progressing SOD1-ALS: arimoclomol was safe, and survival and function trended its way without reaching significance. The planned phase 3 part was dropped because recruitment was slow.

NCT03491462.summary: ORARIALS-01: arimoclomol missed its primary endpoint (function and survival combined) and all secondary endpoints over 76 weeks in 245 patients.

NCT00868166.summary: Olesoxime gave no survival benefit at 18 months (69% vs 68% alive) in 512 patients taking riluzole.

NCT01285583.summary: Open-label safety extension of the olesoxime phase 3, which showed no benefit.

NCT00965497.summary: Small open-label study (13 patients) of escitalopram for depression in people with ALS or MS. No results were posted or found.

NCT01016522.summary: Safety study of a ketogenic tube-feed diet. Only one patient enrolled, and the study was stopped for low enrollment.

NCT00876772.summary: Olanzapine for appetite loss and weight loss. No published results were found; the EU trials register lists a results section.

NCT01281189.summary: EMPOWER: dexpramipexole had no effect on function or survival in 943 patients, and Biogen ended its development in ALS.

NCT01933321.summary: Open-label study of the patient's own blood stem cells given into the spinal fluid (14 patients). No results were posted or found.

NCT01583088.summary: Stopped early: patients given diaphragm pacing with ventilation died sooner than those on ventilation alone. Diaphragm pacing is not recommended in ALS.

NCT01160263.summary: Brain imaging (SPECT) study, not a treatment trial.

NCT01825551.summary: Five days of G-CSF did not slow progression over 3 months in 40 patients; women given G-CSF declined faster than those on placebo.

NCT01776970.summary: CANALS: nabiximols (THC/CBD mouth spray) reduced spasticity over 6 weeks in 59 patients with ALS or primary lateral sclerosis. A symptom treatment; the authors called for larger trials.

NCT02588677.summary: Masitinib met its primary endpoint in the prespecified 'normal progressor' group (27% slower decline over 48 weeks) but not across all patients. It has not been approved, and a confirmatory phase 3 was required.

NCT01994109.summary: RimabotulinumtoxinB (Myobloc) reduced drooling compared with placebo in 187 adults with drooling from several causes; 12 had ALS.

NCT02496767.summary: VITALITY-ALS: tirasemtiv did not slow the decline in breathing capacity, and many patients stopped it because of side effects (34% vs 12% on placebo).

NCT02936635.summary: Open-label extension of tirasemtiv; development stopped after VITALITY-ALS failed.

NCT02623699.summary: VALOR: tofersen did not significantly slow functional decline at 28 weeks, but it sharply lowered SOD1 and neurofilament light, a marker of nerve damage. On that biomarker evidence it received FDA accelerated approval (Qalsody) in 2023.

NCT03070119.summary: Open-label extension of VALOR. Patients who started tofersen earlier declined less by 52 weeks than those who started later (exploratory).

NCT03068754.summary: PENNANT: stopped in 2019 because more patients developed pneumonia on Acthar Gel than on placebo, and too few had reached the endpoint to judge efficacy.

NCT03280056.summary: NurOwn (MSC-NTF cells): 34.7% of treated patients responded vs 27.7% on placebo, not a significant difference. FDA advisers later voted against approval.

NCT03505021.summary: REFALS: oral levosimendan did not slow the decline in breathing capacity at 12 weeks, nor overall function, in 496 patients.

NCT03293069.summary: FAIR-ALS II: deferiprone (iron chelation) vs placebo over 12 months. No results were posted or found in a search in November 2026.

NCT04436510.summary: HEALEY Regimen B: verdiperstat showed no difference from placebo on disease progression.

NCT04436497.summary: HEALEY Regimen A: zilucoplan was stopped early for futility, with no meaningful slowing of progression.

NCT04414345.summary: HEALEY Regimen C: CNM-Au8 missed its primary and secondary endpoints at 24 weeks. Exploratory analyses suggested longer survival at the 30 mg dose, which the RESTORE-ALS phase 3 is designed to test.

NCT04615923.summary: HEALEY Regimen D: pridopidine had no effect on functional decline over 24 weeks. Later analyses in faster-progressing patients led to the PREVAiLS phase 3.

NCT05136885.summary: HEALEY Regimen E: IV trehalose (SLS-005) missed its primary endpoint overall; a prespecified subgroup not taking AMX0035 declined 22% more slowly.

NCT05740813.summary: HEALEY Regimen F: fosigotifator (ABBV-CLS-7262) missed its primary and secondary endpoints.

NCT05842941.summary: HEALEY Regimen G: DNL343 missed its primary endpoint (function and survival) at 24 weeks.

NCT04516096.summary: Compassionate-use access to AMX0035 for patients who finished earlier Amylyx trials; no efficacy comparison.

NCT05619783.summary: Open-label extension of the PHOENIX phase 3. PHOENIX missed its primary endpoint, and Amylyx withdrew AMX0035 (Relyvrio) from the market in 2024.

NCT04745299.summary: ALSUMMIT: lenzumestrocel (Neuronata-R stem cells) missed its primary endpoint (function and survival) in the overall population. The company reports post hoc benefit in slower-progressing patients.

NCT04944784.summary: COURAGE-ALS: stopped for futility at a planned interim analysis; reldesemtiv did not slow functional decline.

NCT06111014.summary: Continuation study of latozinemab, stopped after its parent phase 3 in frontotemporal dementia due to GRN mutations (INFRONT-3) missed its clinical endpoint.
